name: Boston College
cycle: Fall 2026 / Spring 2027 (page verified August 2026; fall deadline March 15, spring deadline November 1)

prompts.text: Please provide a statement that addresses your reasons for transferring and why you are choosing to apply to Boston College.

notes: Two-part prompt at full personal-statement length, so give real weight to both halves: a concrete, non-blaming account of why the current school cannot deliver the path you want, then a BC-specific answer (named programs, the Core, faculty) that no other school would satisfy. BC's own transfer page routes applicants to the Boston College Transfer Application portal rather than the Common App, so treat this as an institutional application; third-party claims of a 'Common Application for Transfer' at BC are not corroborated by bc.edu.

name: Boston University
cycle: 2026-2027 transfer cycle (verified against BU's live transfer page as of August 2026; BU does not version-label this requirement, and its transfer deadlines page did not resolve)

prompts.text: "We want to learn more about you and your reasons for transferring, in particular what you hope to accomplish at Boston University."

notes: BU publishes NO separate writing supplement for transfers - this single essay is the Common App transfer essay under BU's own instruction, and BU caps it at 600 words rather than the Common App's 650, so trim to BU's number. Two details drive the content: the phrase "what you hope to accomplish at Boston University" makes this a why-BU essay, not a generic why-transfer essay; and because BU requires transfers to apply directly to a specific school or college (no undeclared), the essay should name that college and its specific programs rather than praising BU generally.

notes: Correction to a common error: Caltech does NOT take the Common App or the Coalition App for transfer - its requirements page states it accepts only one application for transfer admission, its own, at apply.caltech.edu. Third-party sites claiming Coalition are stale. The transfer-specific prompt is #2 - it pairs "experiences at your current school" with "ready to take the next step," so it wants evidence the current institution has been exhausted academically, not a complaint about it. Note also that essays are not the binding constraint: Caltech requires math and physics entrance exams (due February 15) plus two recommendations from college math/science/engineering faculty, and admits only for fall ("We do not admit students for the winter or spring terms"). cdsUrl is null: I could not locate a Common Data Set page on any caltech.edu domain - registrar.caltech.edu/records/common-data-set, caltech.edu/about/common-data-set and iro.caltech.edu subpages all returned 404, and iro.caltech.edu mentions the CDS as a data source without linking it. Rather than guess a URL, this is left unverified.

name: Duke
cycle: 2025-26 transfer cycle (Fall 2026 entry); deadline March 15, 2026 - most recent cycle verifiable on Duke's live apply page as of Aug 2026

prompts.text: We would like to understand more about you and your reason(s) for transferring. Why and how did you choose your current or most recent college or university and what do you hope to gain by transferring?

Duke University offers students the opportunity to choose up to three academic pathways through majors, minors, and certificates. Describe how you intend to explore your academic and intellectual interests at Duke University.

notes: Duke explicitly states it will not accept the Common App for transfers this cycle - applicants use the Duke Transfer Application or the Coalition/Scoir app, so the 650-word prompt replaces (not supplements) the usual Common App transfer essay and must carry the full transfer narrative. It asks two separable things - why you chose your current school AND what transferring gains you - so justify the original choice on its own terms before naming the specific gap; the 250-word prompt keys on Duke's 'up to three academic pathways' framing, so name actual majors, minors, and certificates and how they combine.

name: Georgetown
cycle: Fall 2026/Spring 2027 transfer cycle; Transfer Application Supplement due March 1, 2026. Application now closed; the Fall 2027/Spring 2028 transfer application becomes available September 2026
notes: Georgetown does not use the Common App for transfer - note that its Aug 1, 2026 Common App adoption applies only to first-year applicants entering fall 2027, so transfers still use Georgetown's own two-part application. The Supplement's short answer and essay questions unlock only after Part 1 is submitted and are not published anywhere public, so the actionable move is to submit Part 1 as soon as the cycle opens in September purely to read the prompts, and to build the essay around a clean academic record narrative since a Dean's Report and a professor recommendation are also required.

name: Notre Dame
cycle: 2026-27 cycle verified on page (Spring 2027 entry, deadline October 1, 2026; Fall 2027 entry, deadline March 15, 2027)
notes: PARTIAL — the transfer page loaded and its deadlines/cycle are verified, but it published no verbatim supplemental prompt text, so prompts is empty rather than guessed. What the page does establish: a personal statement covering interest in Notre Dame, academic and professional goals, and how transferring advances them — so the essay should braid all three into one causal arc (goal -> what's missing now -> the specific Notre Dame program that closes the gap), not treat them as three separate paragraphs. Confirm the exact prompt wording and word limit in the live Common App before publishing.

name: UNC
notes: UNC has no school-specific supplement this cycle — it removed both short answer questions for 2026-2027 ("We're removing the two short answer supplemental questions"), so the Common App transfer essay is the only prose UNC reads. That essay has to do double duty: carry the reason-for-transfer narrative AND the Carolina-specific evidence a supplement would normally hold, so name the actual major, courses, or 2+2 pathway rather than leaving the choice of UNC implied.

name: UPenn

prompts.text: Please explain your reasons for transferring from your current institution and what you hope to gain by transferring to another institution.
Write a short thank-you note to someone you have not yet thanked and would like to acknowledge. (We encourage you to share this note with that person, if possible, and reflect on the experience!)
How will you explore community at Penn? Consider how Penn will help shape your perspective, and how your experiences and perspective will help shape Penn.
Considering the specific undergraduate school you have selected, describe how you intend to explore your academic and intellectual interests at the University of Pennsylvania.
Common App universal transfer essay (not Penn-specific; required of all Common App transfer applicants).

notes: Penn transfers apply directly into one of four undergraduate schools, and prompt 4 is read against that school specifically — cite courses, faculty, and program structures unique to the College, Engineering, Nursing, or Wharton, because a generic "Penn" answer reads as applying to the wrong place. Note the transfer essay (prompt 1) overlaps heavily with the Common App universal transfer essay, so deliberately split the material: the universal one for the narrative of why you are leaving, prompt 1 for what specifically you cannot get where you are; and keep the thank-you note an actual note to an actual person rather than a disguised achievement essay.

name: Vanderbilt
cycle: 2026-2027 (fall 2027 entry, Feb 15 priority deadline; the prompt page itself does not clearly re-label the cycle, so re-check the live Common App before drafting)

prompts.text: Vanderbilt University's motto, Crescere aude, is Latin for 'dare to grow.' In your response, reflect on how one or more aspects of your identity, culture, or background has played a role in your personal growth, and how it will contribute to our campus community as you dare to grow at Vanderbilt.

notes: The Crescere aude short answer is an identity-and-growth prompt, not a "why Vanderbilt" prompt — the transfer rationale belongs in the Common App essay, which Vanderbilt explicitly wants answering why Vanderbilt and why now. At roughly 250 words, commit to one aspect of background and trace it to one concrete way you would contribute on campus; the prompt's two-part structure (growth, then contribution) means an essay that only does the reflection half is incomplete.

name: Washington
cycle: 2026-2027 transfer cycle (verified against UW's live transfer pages as of August 2026; UW does not version-label the personal statement prompt)

prompts.text: "Your personal statement should be a comprehensive narrative essay outlining significant aspects of your academic and personal history, particularly those that provide context for your academic achievements and educational choices."

notes: UW does not use the Common App for transfer at all - applicants use UW's own online transfer application, so there is no 650-word Common App essay to reuse. The single personal statement is unusually long (750-1,000 suggested, roughly 50% longer than a Common App essay) because it is a checklist in narrative form: UW asks it to cover college performance to date and the educational path taken, any situations that significantly affected academic progress, reasons for leaving the current institution, the intended major and career goals with a plan for completing prerequisites, second-choice major goals if one is listed, and explicitly "How will the UW help you attain your academic, career and personal goals?" Optional additions include educational challenges or personal hardship, community service, experiential learning, and any compelling need for the Seattle campus. Structure the essay to hit every required element - a beautiful essay that skips the prerequisite plan or the reason for leaving reads as incomplete. Deadlines vary by quarter; February 15 is the common Autumn deadline.

name: Wisconsin
cycle: 2026-2027 transfer cycle (Spring 2027 and Fall 2027 entry; deadlines published as Oct 1 for Spring 2027, Feb 1 priority / Mar 1 regular for Fall 2027)

prompts.text: "Each student is unique. Please tell us about the particular life experiences, talents, commitments, and/or interests you will bring to our campus."
prompts.words: 650 words maximum, 300-500 recommended (per admissions.wisc.edu/apply/essays; no limit restated on the transfer page)

prompts.text: "Tell us why you would like to attend the University of Wisconsin-Madison. In addition, please include why you are interested in studying the major(s) you have selected."
prompts.words: 650 words maximum, 300-500 recommended (per admissions.wisc.edu/apply/essays; no limit restated on the transfer page)

notes: Important correction to the usual assumption: UW-Madison accepts the Common App for first-year applicants but NOT for transfers - transfer applicants use the Universities of Wisconsin Application at apply.wisconsin.edu, so there is no Common App transfer essay in play and both essays below are the entire writing requirement. The first prompt is waived for applicants transferring in from another Universities of Wisconsin institution, who submit only the second. The second prompt is the one that decides files because it is two questions welded together - why Madison AND why this major - and the "In addition" clause means an essay that only sells the university has answered half the question. Name specific Madison courses, faculty, labs or program features tied to the declared major. Note UW-Madison's own essay page recommends 300-500 words against a 650 ceiling, so the recommended length is well short of the maximum.
